title: Reconcile token accounting when edge proxies rewrite or normalize prompts
creator: Arielle Park
description:
Background:
Many customers route requests through third-party gateways, internal edge proxies, or API management layers that perform prompt rewriting: templating, instruction enrichment, anonymization, or HTTP->gRPC transformation. These rewrites can change the exact bytes presented to our tokenizer (whitespace normalization, unicode normalization, instruction prepending, JSON escaping), producing a different token count than what the client-side SDK or UI estimated.

Problem statement:
- Mismatched token counts between client estimates and server meter make debugging billing disputes hard.
- Some rewrites inject short but token-expensive constructs (e.g., verbose JSON escaping, instruction scaffolding) causing unexpectedly higher charges.
- Other proxies strip or compress parts of the payload, producing undercounts and downstream heuristics that assume client length.
- Current logs only contain final canonical text (post-rewrite) used for metering; we lack a structured way to attribute tokens to original vs injected content for audit/refund workflows.

User impact:
- Revenue disputes for customers reporting higher-than-expected usage (customer_impact: medium).
- Increased support load for SRE and billing ops to triage and compensate legitimate customers.

Scope:
- Ingress path: edge proxy (customer-controlled or partner) -> gateway -> API frontend -> tokenizer -> metering ledger.
- Focus on text-based generation/chat/structured-output requests in streaming and non-streaming flows.
- Exclude audio transcription pipelines in initial implementation (follow-up ticket to add).
proposed_solution:
Design summary:
1) Canonicalization step in server ingress that is deterministic and shared with SDKs: apply NFKC unicode normalization, consistent newline normalization, and JSON/string unescape rules.
2) Compute a lightweight origin map: produce a short mapping describing which spans of the canonicalized text correspond to client-supplied input vs runtime/edge-injected content. Store span metadata as small tag arrays in the metering ledger (tag values are short strings like 'client', 'proxy-insert', 'gateway-sanitized').
3) Accept optional client header X-Client-Canonical-Hash (SHA256 of client-preprocessed-canonical-string) emitted by updated SDKs to help fast-match and short-circuit diffs for compatible clients. If header present and hash matches server canonicalization result, attribute tokens to 'client' wholesale.
4) When diffs exceed a threshold (e.g., token delta > 5% or > 10 tokens), emit a structured incident in billing-audit pipeline and surface on the "ingress-rewrite-drift" dashboard.
5) Add reconciliation automation for small deltas: automatically issue prorated credits when server detects clear proxy-injection (e.g., recognized gateway signature and deterministic injection template).

Implementation notes:
- Avoid storing large per-request mappings in full; store compressed span summaries (max ~256 bytes per request) to keep ledger costs bounded.
- Use the existing tokenizer service to compute tokenization but ensure canonicalizer is run before tokenization to avoid inconsistencies.
- SDK rollout: ship canonicalization helper in JS/Python/Go SDKs that computes the canonical hash and optionally passes X-Client-Canonical-Hash and X-Client-Token-Estimate headers. SDKs will be best-effort backward compatible; server must not rely on header presence.
- Streaming: calculate attribution incrementally for each chunk. For streamed requests with midstream proxy rewrites (e.g., instruction appended after connection), tag late-inserted tokens as 'runtime-insert' and preserve original client-attributed tokens.

Trade-offs considered:
- Full provenance mapping is accurate but expensive in storage/IO. We opt for compact span summaries and heuristics for automatic credits.
- Relying on client headers speeds common-case reconciliation but creates a dependency on SDK upgrades; server-side canonicalization is the fallback.
- Automatic crediting reduces support load but must be conservative to avoid fraud; initial rules will be narrow and reviewed by billing ops.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests for canonicalizer produce deterministic outputs across platforms (JS/Python/Go).
E2E test simulating common proxy rewrites (templating, escaping, whitespace) shows ledger attribution tags and token deltas in expected ranges.
Dashboard ingests 'ingress-rewrite-drift' metric with per-tenant percent-delta and alert at >1% of requests above threshold for any tenant.
SDKs can emit X-Client-Canonical-Hash and match reduces reconciliation time on canary tenants.
Billing ops runbook created: steps to query ledger span tags and issue prorated credits for qualifying diffs.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (canary): implement server canonicalizer + compact span tagging and enable for 10 internal tenants (2/10 -> 2/24). Monitor drift and perf.
Phase 2 (SDK opt-in): release SDK canonicalizer helpers and encourage customers to enable X-Client-Canonical-Hash (3/10 tenants opt-in -> 3/15).
Phase 3 (automation): deploy small-prorate automation for deterministic injection signatures (3/25).
Phase 4 (full roll): enable span tagging platform-wide and add billing refund automation rules after 2 weeks of stable metrics (4/05).
